claim_text: The education ministry says a third party got unauthorised access to its government procurement system
summary: Japan's education ministry (MEXT) says unauthorised access by a third party was detected on Oct 1, 2026, on servers that make up its government procurement information system.
detail: The ministry says it investigated with an outside specialist organisation. It has not said how the attacker got in.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's Nov 25 notice: unauthorised access by a third party (第三者による不正アクセス) was detected on Oct 1, 2026, on servers of its government procurement information system; The Record reports the Oct 1 detection.

claim_text: Up to 1,778 email addresses and up to 163,953 company and representative records may have leaked
summary: MEXT says email addresses (up to 1,778) and companies' names, their representatives' names and other details (up to 163,953 records) stored in the system's database may have leaked.
detail: The ministry gives these as the figures it can confirm so far. The Record rounds them to nearly 1,700 email addresses and 164,000 records.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's Nov 25 notice lists email addresses stored in the database, up to 1,778 (最大1,778件), and company names and representatives' names and so on, up to 163,953 (最大163,953件); The Record reports the same data in round figures.

claim_text: The ministry has cut off the system's communications
summary: MEXT says communications in and out of the system that was accessed have already been cut off.
detail: The notice does not say whether the procurement system itself is offline, or whether bidders' use of it was affected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's notice: 不正アクセスのあったシステムの内外通信については既に遮断済みです (communications in and out of the affected system are already blocked); The Record reports the ministry blocked all communications between the system and internal and external networks.

claim_text: The ministry has found no publication or misuse of the data so far
summary: MEXT says that, so far, it has found no sign that the data was published to the public or misused.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's notice says no damage has been confirmed at present, such as the possibly leaked information being made public or used improperly; The Record reports no evidence the data was disclosed or misused.

claim_text: The ministry has reported the leak to Japan's privacy regulator and is still investigating
summary: MEXT says it has reported the matter to the Personal Information Protection Commission, Japan's privacy regulator, and is investigating with the relevant bodies. It says it will look for the cause and strengthen its security.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's notice: 本件は個人情報保護委員会へ報告済み (reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission), investigation continuing with relevant bodies; The Record reports it was reported to Japan's data protection authorities.

claim_text: The ministry has not said who was behind the intrusion or how it happened
summary: MEXT has not named an attacker or said how the intruder got in. No group has been publicly linked to the intrusion in the reporting found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's notice describes only unauthorised access by a third party and says the cause is still being investigated; The Record reports the ministry has not publicly identified the perpetrators and does not say how the hackers gained access.

claim_text: The ministry disclosed the intrusion nearly two months after detecting it
summary: MEXT detected the intrusion on Oct 1, 2026, and published its notice on Nov 25, 2026, nearly two months later.
detail: The notice does not say why it was published then.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's notice is dated Nov 25, 2026 (令和8年11月25日) and gives Oct 1, 2026 as the date the access was detected; The Record notes the ministry detected the intrusion nearly two months before disclosing it.

claim_text: The system publishes information on government tenders and contracts
summary: According to The Record, the system publishes information about government tenders, contracts and procurement opportunities, and the business information exposed relates to companies eligible for the ministry's bidding.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Record (Nov 27) describes the system as publishing information about government tenders, contracts and procurement opportunities, and says the exposed data relates to companies eligible for the ministry's bidding.
notes: MEXT's notice does not describe the system's purpose.

claim_text: MEXT is the Japanese government ministry for education, science, sports and culture
summary: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) was formed in 2001 from the Ministry of Education, Science, Sports and Culture and the Science and Technology Agency.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: MEXT's own chronology page: 2001, MEXT established by merging the Ministry of Education, Science, Sports and Culture and the Science and Technology Agency.
